pitRules: Draft publication, comment-end, final publication and effective date are separate clocks.
Retroactive legal effect never backdates market observability.
Later amendments append new policy vintages and do not overwrite earlier known state.
Surprise requires a compatible ex-ante expectation source captured before the decision; otherwise surprise=UNKNOWN.
Market reaction cannot be reverse-engineered into expectation or surprise.
counterevidence: Final publication need not equal effective date.
Effective date can precede publication or vary by provision.
Draft language can change before final rule.
A draft-only item is not a final policy event.
No ex-ante expectation archive is validated here, so surprise remains UNKNOWN.
No market return outcome was inspected.
